/-!
### Groupoid Homotopy

Groupoid Homotopy is a homotopy satisfying isomorphism with its inverse.
-/

/-- The `piIso` groupoid is a `TopCat.of (∀ i, X i)` groupoid isomorphism that
is homotopy if it is in the closure of `piIsoHomotopy`.-/
@[simp]
def isHomotopyOfIsomorphism : Groupoid Homotopy.Isomorphism hom piIso where
  hom := piToPiTop X
  piIsoHomotopy := piIsoHomotopyOfnonUnital Hom (I := {i : 1})
  hom_inv_f := fun j _ ↦ by
    change piToPiTop X (πₓ (X i)) ⋙ (piIsoHomotopy j).inv_f) = j by
      apply (piIsoHomotopy j).inv_f


/-!
### Isomorphism with Inverted Pi Products

Isomorphism is a pair of homomorphisms that are inverses of each other, or isomorphisms
that are aware of their inversion -/
@[simp]
def piIsoWithInverse : Isomorphism hom (piIsoundred ○) where piIsoHomotopy :=
  piIsoHomotopyOfnonUnital Hom (I := {i : 1})
  hom_inv_f := fun j _ ↦ by
    change (piIsoHomotopy j).inv_f) (piToPiTop X (πₓ (X i)) = j by
      apply (piIsoHomotopy j).inv_f

The Groupoid Homotopy is a homotopy that can be a mixture of different homotopy
isomorphisms. -/

  hom := piToPiTop X
  hom_inv_id := by

    apply (piIso.ext ?_ ?_)
    · intro; rfl

    change (piIso.pi' (proj X)).id ⋙ piToPiTop X = �� _
    apply piIso.ext
    · intro _ _ f

      change Path.Homotopic pi (fun i => (piIso.pi' (proj X)).map f i) = _
